title: Eduversal Year-1 Induction Observation Rubric
description: A formative, developmental rubric for the Year-1 Subject Teacher induction observation cycle. The school leader (or mentor, for monthly observations) watches one full lesson and records where the new teacher's practice sits on a four-step developmental progression in each of four domains. This is NOT the network appraisal rubric. It produces NO letter grade, NO numeric score, and NO band. Its only purpose is to describe present practice and name the next step so the new teacher can grow. Used for the Q4 induction-completion observation and for monthly mentor observations during the year.

charter.nn1Statement: Year-1 induction data NEVER feeds network appraisal scoring.
guarantees: Output is a developmental level word (Emerging / Developing / Embedding / Extending) per domain — never a letter band and never a number.
The level a new teacher reaches in induction NEVER migrates into teacher_appraisals or becomes a year-2 KPI baseline.
Findings exist to inform the next coaching conversation, not to rank the teacher.
The observation is recorded in induction_observations only, separate from the appraisal collections by design and by Firestore rule.
If a school leader is tempted to translate these levels into a score, that is an NN1 violation — the levels are deliberately worded so they cannot be summed or averaged.
charter.whyNotAToF: An A-F band or a number invites comparison and ranking, which turns a safe first-year growth process into a hidden performance exam. A new teacher who fears the number stops taking risks and stops asking for help — the opposite of what induction is for. The developmental progression below describes practice without judging the person.

developmentalLevels.label: Emerging
developmentalLevels.description: The practice is just beginning to appear. The new teacher is aware of what good practice looks like but does it inconsistently, with prompting, or in part. This is a normal and expected place for a teacher to be early in the year.
developmentalLevels.coachingFrame: Name one small, concrete thing to try in the next lesson. Model it together first.

developmentalLevels.label: Developing
developmentalLevels.description: The practice is present and growing. The new teacher does it in most lessons but it is not yet automatic — it still takes conscious effort and the quality varies between lessons.
developmentalLevels.coachingFrame: Help the teacher make the practice steadier. Look at the lessons where it worked and ask what was different.

developmentalLevels.label: Embedding
developmentalLevels.description: The practice is becoming a routine. The new teacher does it reliably, without prompting, and it is starting to feel natural. The expected endpoint of a successful first year.
developmentalLevels.coachingFrame: Confirm and celebrate the routine. Ask the teacher to notice when they use it and why it helps students.

developmentalLevels.label: Extending
developmentalLevels.description: The practice is secure AND the teacher is beginning to adapt it for different students, contexts, or content. This is above what a first year requires — recognise it, do not expect it.
developmentalLevels.coachingFrame: Invite the teacher to share the practice with peers and to keep stretching it in year 2.

levelNote: The four levels are a developmental progression, NOT a 4-point scale. Do not add them up, do not average them across domains, do not convert them to a percentage. A teacher who finishes the year mostly at 'Developing' with one domain 'Embedding' has had a successful induction. 'Extending' is a bonus, never a target.

domains.title: Planning
domains.guidingQuestion: Is the lesson planned so that students can reach a clear learning goal?
domains.lookFor: A clear learning objective, lesson steps that build toward it, content that is accurate and matched to the syllabus, and resources prepared in advance.

levelDescriptors.emerging: The lesson has a goal, but the steps do not always connect to it, or the plan is mostly in the teacher's head. Timing and resources are improvised.
levelDescriptors.developing: The lesson has a clear objective and a logical sequence in most lessons. The teacher is starting to anticipate where students might struggle and to plan for it.
levelDescriptors.embedding: Lessons are reliably planned with a clear objective, a coherent sequence, accurate content tied to the syllabus, and resources ready. The teacher routinely plans for likely misconceptions.
levelDescriptors.extending: Plans are secure and the teacher adapts them for different starting points — planning more than one route to the same objective for students who need it.

domains.title: Classroom Management
domains.guidingQuestion: Is the classroom a calm, respectful, ready-to-learn environment?
domains.lookFor: Clear and fair routines, positive relationships with all students, time used well, low-level disruption handled calmly, and every student feeling safe to take part.

levelDescriptors.emerging: Routines exist but are applied unevenly. Some time is lost to transitions or off-task behaviour. The teacher is still finding a consistent, calm voice.
levelDescriptors.developing: Routines are mostly clear and applied fairly. Relationships with students are positive. The teacher manages most low-level disruption without losing the lesson's momentum.
levelDescriptors.embedding: The classroom runs on reliable routines. Relationships are warm and respectful, expectations are high and consistent, and time is protected for learning. Disruption is rare and handled calmly.
levelDescriptors.extending: Management is secure and the teacher adapts it to the group — adjusting routines for different classes and pre-empting issues before they arise.

domains.title: Instruction
domains.guidingQuestion: Are the teaching strategies helping all students learn and stay engaged?
domains.lookFor: Clear explanations, good questioning, appropriate pace, strategies that motivate and challenge, and content delivered so that all students — including those who need support or stretch — can access it.

levelDescriptors.emerging: Explanations are sometimes unclear or too fast/slow. Questioning is mostly closed and directed to a few students. The teacher relies on one main strategy.
levelDescriptors.developing: Explanations are clear in most lessons. The teacher uses a mix of questions and starts to check more students' understanding. Pace is generally appropriate.
levelDescriptors.embedding: Explanations are consistently clear, questioning draws in the whole class and probes thinking, pace is well-judged, and strategies motivate and challenge students across the ability range.
levelDescriptors.extending: Instruction is secure and the teacher adapts strategies in the moment — reading the room, changing approach when students are stuck, and stretching those who are ready.

domains.title: Assessment for Learning
domains.guidingQuestion: Does the teacher check what students have understood and act on it?
domains.lookFor: Checking understanding during the lesson, responding to what is found, timely and useful feedback, and using what students show to decide the next step.

levelDescriptors.emerging: The teacher checks understanding mainly at the end, or assumes it. Feedback is general ('good', 'try harder') rather than specific. Next steps are not yet shaped by what students show.
levelDescriptors.developing: The teacher checks understanding during the lesson in most cases and begins to adjust. Feedback is becoming more specific. Some next steps are informed by what students did.
levelDescriptors.embedding: The teacher checks understanding throughout, responds to it in the lesson, gives timely and constructive feedback, and routinely uses what students show to plan the next step.
levelDescriptors.extending: Assessment is secure and the teacher uses a range of strategies fluidly — adapting checks for different students and weaving feedback into instruction without breaking flow.

narrativeFields.label: Glow — what went well
narrativeFields.description: The clearest strength of this lesson. Specific and evidence-anchored. This is what the teacher should keep doing.

narrativeFields.label: Grow — the one next step
narrativeFields.description: The single most useful next step before the next observation. Specific, doable, framed as growth — never a list of deficits.

narrativeFields.label: Go — what we agreed to try
narrativeFields.description: The concrete action the teacher and observer agreed on in the post-conference, with any support the mentor or school leader will provide.

narrativeFields.label: Teacher's own reflection
narrativeFields.description: The new teacher's own thoughts on the lesson and the agreed next step, in their own words. Optional but encouraged.

useContexts.label: Q4 induction-completion observation
useContexts.note: The mentee's induction-completion observation. Recorded in induction_observations with type='formal_evaluation'. Charter NN1: output stays in induction_observations and NEVER auto-migrates to teacher_appraisals or a year-2 KPI baseline.

useContexts.label: Monthly mentor observation
useContexts.note: The same rubric supports the mentor's regular formative observations across the year, so the Q4 observation uses a familiar instrument. Always developmental, never scored.

cambridgeTeacherStandards2023.note: Domain descriptors anchor to CTS 2023 Standards 2 (relationships/environment) and 3 (teaching and learning). Year-1 teacher is expected to show awareness-to-routine, not mastery.

cambridgeICTL5881.note: Units 1-3 underpin the Planning, Instruction, and Assessment domains; the rubric mirrors the ICTL effective-lesson framing the mentee studies in stages 1-2.

eduversalAcademicStandards.note: ES 7.4 (Observation and Feedback Process), ES 7.5 / 12.5 (New Teacher Induction Program). The Glow/Grow/Go structure satisfies ES 7.4's feedback-process expectation.

pigp_27_2010.note: PIGP pasal-9 + lampiran D-1 require a structured observation of the beginning teacher; this rubric satisfies and exceeds that mandate while keeping induction data out of formal appraisal.

skl_10_2025.note: Domains tag the SKL graduate-profile dimensions (penalaran_kritis, kemandirian) the observed lesson should help develop.
